steps.stem: The vertices of triangle \(ABC\) are \(A(5,\ 16)\), \(B(-19,\ {-}8)\) and \(C(12,\ {-}8)\). What is its perimeter?
explanation: \(B\) and \(C\) have the same \(y\) (\(-8\)). So, \(BC\) is horizontal: \(BC=19+12=31\).
Drop the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\). Its foot is \(H(5,\ {-}8)\), and \(AH=16+8=24\).
Left: \(BH=19+5=24\) and \(AH=24\). This is a 45-45-90 triangle. So, \(AB=24\sqrt2\).
Right: \(HC=12-5=7\) and \(AH=24\). This is the triple 7-24-25. So, \(AC=25\).
Perimeter: \(31+25+24\sqrt2=56+24\sqrt2\).
Traps: \(55+24\sqrt2\) uses the altitude (24) instead of \(AC\), and \(80\) takes \(AB\) as 24.

steps.stem: The vertices of triangle \(ABC\) are \(A(-2,\ 1)\), \(B(4,\ {-}1)\) and \(C(2,\ 5)\). What is the area of the triangle?
explanation: No side is horizontal or vertical. So, draw a box around the triangle with sides parallel to the axes.
The box goes from \(x=-2\) to \(x=4\) (width 6) and from \(y=-1\) to \(y=5\) (height 6). Its area is \(6\cdot6=36\).

Three right triangles fill the corners of the box outside \(ABC\). \(A\) to \(B\): 6 across and 2 down, \(\frac{6\cdot2}{2}=6\). \(B\) to \(C\): 2 across and 6 up, \(\frac{2\cdot6}{2}=6\). \(C\) to \(A\): 4 across and 4 down, \(\frac{4\cdot4}{2}=8\).

steps.stem: A circle with radius \(8\) is centered at the origin \(O\). The point \(A\) lies on the circle in the first quadrant, and its \(y\)-coordinate is \(4\). What is the angle between \(OA\) and the positive \(x\)-axis?
explanation: Drop \(AH\) perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis. \(AH=4\) (the \(y\) of \(A\)) and \(OA=8\) (a radius).
In a right triangle, a leg that is half the hypotenuse faces a \(30°\) angle (the 30-60-90 triangle).
So \(\angle AOH=30°\).

steps.stem: \(M(2,\ {-}1)\) is the midpoint of segment \(AB\). Given: \(A(-4,\ 3)\). What are the coordinates of \(B\)?
explanation: From \(A(-4,\ 3)\) to \(M(2,\ {-}1)\): 6 right and 4 down.
\(M\) is the middle. So, \(B\) is the same move again from \(M\): \(B=(2+6,\ {-}1-4)=(8,\ {-}5)\).
Check with the averages: \(\frac{-4+8}{2}=2\) and \(\frac{3+(-5)}{2}=-1\). That is \(M\).

steps.stem: The line \(4x+3y=24\) intersects the \(x\)-axis at \(A\) and the \(y\)-axis at \(B\). What is the length of \(AB\)?
explanation: \(OA=6\) and \(OB=8\) are the legs of a right triangle with the right angle at \(O\). \(AB\) is the hypotenuse: 6-8-10. So, \(AB=10\).
Traps: \(14=6+8\) adds the legs, and \(24=\frac{6\cdot8}{2}\) is the area.

steps.stem: A straight line passes through the origin and through \(A(-3p,\ {-}3q)\), where \(p>0\), \(q>0\) and \(p\ne q\). The point \(B\) lies on this line in the first quadrant. Which of the following cannot be the coordinates of \(B\)?
explanation: The line passes through the origin. So, every point on it has the same ratio \(\frac xy\). For \(A\): \(\frac{-3p}{-3q}=\frac pq\).
Check the choices: \(\frac{2p}{2q}=\frac pq\), \(\ \frac1q\div\frac1p=\frac pq\) and \(\frac{p/3}{q/3}=\frac pq\). These three can be on the line.
\(\frac{p^3}{q^3}=\frac pq\) only if \(p^2=q^2\), that is \(p=q\) (both are positive). But \(p\ne q\). So, \((p^3,\ q^3)\) cannot be on the line.

Quick check with numbers: \(p=1\), \(q=2\). The line goes through \((1,\ 2)\). So, \(y\) is always twice \(x\). \((1,\ 8)\) is not on it; \((2,\ 4)\), \((\frac12,\ 1)\) and \((\frac13,\ \frac23)\) are.

steps.title: The coordinate plane — what to know
steps.intro: On the plane, it's still geometry: find lengths from the values, then use Pythagoras and the special triangles.

head: Situation
What to do
rows: \(A(x,\ y)\) — \(x\) first, \(y\) second · on the \(x\)-axis \(y=0\), on the \(y\)-axis \(x=0\)
I \((+,+)\) · II \((-,+)\) · III \((-,-)\) · IV \((+,-)\) · a point on an axis is in no quadrant
across the \(x\)-axis \((x,\ -y)\) · across the \(y\)-axis \((-x,\ y)\) · through the origin \((-x,\ -y)\)
vertical segment (parallel to the \(y\)-axis) — use the \(y\) values
horizontal segment (parallel to the \(x\)-axis) — use the \(x\) values
same side: subtract · opposite sides: add the two parts
lines parallel to the axes → right triangle → Pythagoras (triples, silver, golden)
the average of the \(x\) values, the average of the \(y\) values · or repeat the move from one end
box it in (sides parallel to the axes), subtract the corner right triangles
it is parallel to that axis
find \(r\) first · tangent to both axes: center \((r,\ r)\) · center at \(O\): radius to the point + Pythagoras
constant slope: equal pieces = identical steps (same across, same up)
the same slope: the same step across and the same step up
\(y=mx+b\): \(m\) = slope, \(b\) = where it cuts the \(y\)-axis · \(x\)-axis: put \(y=0\) · \(y\)-axis: put \(x=0\)
\(x:y\) is the same for every point — both values × the same number

tips: Never mind the distance formula — it is just Pythagoras.
A center at \((5,\ 0)\) does not mean \(r=5\) — subtract the \(x\) of a point on the circle.
A leg equal to half the hypotenuse → a \(30°\)-\(60°\)-\(90°\) triangle; the \(30°\) faces the short leg.
Answers given as roots? Compare across\(^2+\) up\(^2\) with the number under the root. No need to take the root.
Letters in the question? Plug in easy numbers (for example \(a=1\), \(b=2\)) and check each choice.

steps.stem: A rectangle has sides parallel to the coordinate axes. Two opposite vertices of the rectangle are \((-4,\ 2)\) and \((2,\ 9)\). The rectangle makes a full turn around its right-hand vertical side. What is the volume of the solid formed?
explanation: The width is \(2-(-4)=6\) and the height is \(9-2=7\).
A full turn around the right side gives a cylinder. Its radius is the width, \(r=6\), and its height is \(h=7\).
\(V=\pi r^2h=\pi\cdot36\cdot7=252\pi\).
Traps: \(63\pi\) takes half the width as the radius, and \(294\pi\) swaps the radius and the height.

steps.stem: \(ABCD\) is a right trapezoid with \(AD\parallel BC\). Side \(DC\) is parallel to the \(y\)-axis, and \(AB\) passes through the origin \(E\). Given: \(A(4,\ 3)\), \(D(10,\ 3)\) and \(AE=EB\). What is the area of the trapezoid?
explanation: \(E\) is the origin and the midpoint of \(AB\). From \(E\) to \(A\): 4 right and 3 up. So from \(E\) to \(B\): 4 left and 3 down. \(B=(-4,\ {-}3)\).
The height is \(DC=3+3=6\).
Traps: \(36\) is only the \(6\times6\) rectangle, \(48\) takes \(BC\) as 10, and \(120\) forgets to divide by 2.

steps.stem: A circle is centered at the origin \(O\) and passes through \(A(8,\ 8)\). \(B\) is the point where the circle meets the negative \(y\)-axis. The two shaded regions together are the right half of the circle without triangle \(OAB\). What is their total area?
explanation: Radius: from \(O\) to \(A(8,\ 8)\) is 8 right and 8 up, a 45-45-90 triangle. So \(r=8\sqrt2\) and \(r^2=128\).
The right half of the circle: \(\frac{128\pi}{2}=64\pi\).
Triangle \(OAB\): the base \(OB=8\sqrt2\) is a radius on the \(y\)-axis. The altitude to it is the distance from \(A\) to the \(y\)-axis, 8. Area: \(\frac{8\sqrt2\cdot8}{2}=32\sqrt2\).
Shaded area: \(64\pi-32\sqrt2\).

steps.stem: \(ABCDEF\) is a regular hexagon. Side \(CD\) lies on the positive \(x\)-axis, \(B\) lies on the positive \(y\)-axis, and \(C=(4,\ 0)\). The whole hexagon is shaded except triangle \(AFE\). What is the shaded area?
explanation: Each angle of a regular hexagon is \(120°\). So, \(\angle BCO=180°-120°=60°\).
Triangle \(BOC\) is a 30-60-90 triangle with short leg \(OC=4\). So the side of the hexagon is \(BC=2\cdot4=8\).
The hexagon is 6 equilateral triangles with side 8. Each has area \(\frac{8^2\sqrt3}{4}=16\sqrt3\). Triangle \(AFE\) has the same area as one of them.
Shaded area: \(5\cdot16\sqrt3=80\sqrt3\).

steps.stem: Line \(n\) passes through the origin and through \(C(8,\ 6)\). Line \(m\) is parallel to \(n\) and passes through \(A(4,\ 10)\) and \(B(0,\ b)\). What are the coordinates of \(B\)?
explanation: Line \(n\): from \(O\) to \(C(8,\ 6)\) is 8 right and 6 up.
Line \(m\) is parallel to \(n\). So, it has the same steps: 4 right goes with \(\frac{6}{8}\cdot4=3\) up.
From \(B\) (on the \(y\)-axis) to \(A(4,\ 10)\) is 4 right. So, 3 up. Then \(b=10-3=7\) and \(B=(0,\ 7)\).

steps.stem: A straight line and the \(x\)-axis have some number of points in common. Which of the following cannot be that number?
explanation: A slanted line or a vertical line meets the \(x\)-axis once: 1 point.
The \(x\)-axis itself: infinitely many points.
A line parallel to the \(x\)-axis (and not on it) never meets it: 0 points.
A straight line can never meet the \(x\)-axis in exactly 3 points.

steps.stem: Straight line \(a\) does not intersect the \(y\)-axis, and straight line \(b\) does not intersect the \(x\)-axis. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: If \((-6,\ 1)\) lies on \(a\), then \((6,\ 1)\) also lies on \(a\).
If \((-6,\ 1)\) lies on \(a\), then \((-6,\ {-}7)\) also lies on \(a\).
If \((2,\ {-}3)\) lies on \(b\), then \((-2,\ 3)\) also lies on \(b\).
If \((2,\ {-}3)\) lies on \(b\), then \((2,\ 3)\) also lies on \(b\).
explanation: Line \(a\) never meets the \(y\)-axis. So, it is parallel to it (vertical). Every point on \(a\) has the same \(x\).
If \((-6,\ 1)\) is on \(a\), then every point on \(a\) has \(x=-6\). So \((-6,\ {-}7)\) is on \(a\): choice 2 is true.
Choice 1 changes \(x\). So, it is false.
Line \(b\) is horizontal. If \((2,\ {-}3)\) is on \(b\), every point on \(b\) has \(y=-3\). Choices 3 and 4 change \(y\). So, they are false.

steps.stem: A straight line passes through \((3,\ {-}5)\). It is not perpendicular to either of the coordinate axes. Which of the following points cannot lie on the line?
explanation: The line is not perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis. So, it is not vertical. It is not perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis. So, it is not horizontal.
\((-1,\ {-}5)\) has the same \(y\) as \((3,\ {-}5)\). The line through both points is horizontal, which is not allowed.
Each other point has a different \(x\) and a different \(y\) from \((3,\ {-}5)\). The line through it is slanted. So, it is possible.

steps.stem: Which pair of points lies on a line parallel to the \(y\)-axis?
explanation: A line parallel to the \(y\)-axis is vertical: all its points have the same \(x\).
Only \((4,\ {-}1)\) and \((4,\ 6)\) have the same \(x\), 4. Trap: choice 3 has the same \(y\), so it is parallel to the \(x\)-axis.

steps.stem: The point \(P(-7,\ 3)\) is reflected across the \(y\)-axis to \(Q\). What are the coordinates of \(Q\)?
explanation: A reflection across the \(y\)-axis changes the sign of \(x\) and keeps \(y\): \((x,\ y)\rightarrow(-x,\ y)\).

steps.stem: What is the shortest distance from the point \(P(-3,\ 7)\) to the line \(y=-2\)?
explanation: \(y=-2\) is a horizontal line. The shortest way from \(P\) to it is straight down (vertical).

steps.stem: A circle has center \((3,\ {-}4)\) and is tangent to the \(x\)-axis. What is the area of the circle?
explanation: The circle is tangent to the \(x\)-axis. So, the radius to the point of tangency is vertical. Its length is the distance from the center to the \(x\)-axis: 4 (the \(y\) of the center without the sign).
Area \(=\pi\cdot4^2=16\pi\).

steps.stem: For which pair of points does the straight line through them pass through the origin?
explanation: On a line through the origin, you get from one point to another by multiplying both coordinates by the same number.
\((4,\ {-}6)\cdot(-1.5)=(-6,\ 9)\). Both coordinates are multiplied by \(-1.5\). So, the line through these points passes through the origin.
The other pairs share a coordinate: choice 1 is the vertical line \(x=4\), and choices 3 and 4 are the horizontal lines \(y=9\) and \(y=-6\). None of them passes through the origin.

steps.stem: A circle has its center on the \(x\)-axis and passes through the origin. Which line is tangent to the circle at the origin?
explanation: The center is on the \(x\)-axis. So, the radius to the origin lies on the \(x\)-axis.
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point where it touches the circle. The line through the origin that is perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis is the \(y\)-axis.

steps.stem: A circle has center \(A(15,\ 0)\) and radius \(17\). It intersects the positive \(y\)-axis at \((0,\ y)\). What is \(y\)?
explanation: Join the center \(A(15,\ 0)\) to the point \((0,\ y)\). With the origin, they make a right triangle.
The horizontal leg is 15, and the hypotenuse is a radius, 17. So the other leg is 8 (the triple 8-15-17).
The point is on the positive \(y\)-axis. So, \(y=8\).

steps.stem: A straight line passes through \((5,\ {-}3)\) and does not intersect the \(x\)-axis. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: The point \((-3,\ 5)\) lies on the line.
The line passes through the origin.
The line is perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis.
The point \((5,\ 3)\) lies on the line.
explanation: A whole straight line that never meets the \(x\)-axis must be parallel to it. Therefore it is horizontal: every point on it has \(y=-3\).
A horizontal line is perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis: choice 3.
The other choices: \((-3,\ 5)\), \((5,\ 3)\) and the origin \((0,\ 0)\) do not have \(y=-3\). So, they are not on the line.

steps.stem: A straight line intersects the \(x\)-axis at exactly one point, and that point is not the origin. The line is not perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: The line and the coordinate axes bound a rectangle.
The line and the coordinate axes bound a right triangle.
explanation: The line meets the \(x\)-axis at one point. So, it is not horizontal. It is not perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis. So, it is not vertical. A slanted line meets the \(y\)-axis too, exactly once.
The line does not pass through the origin. So, it meets the two axes at two different points, both away from the origin.
The line and the two axes close a right triangle (the right angle is at the origin).
Choices 1 and 3 are not necessarily true: the line can meet the positive or the negative \(y\)-axis.

steps.stem: Straight lines \(a\) and \(b\) are parallel, and they are not the same line. Line \(a\) passes through the origin, and line \(b\) passes through \((4,\ 0)\). Which point cannot lie on \(a\)?
explanation: If \(a\) passed through \((-5,\ 0)\) and the origin, \(a\) would be the \(x\)-axis.
Then \(a\) would also pass through \((4,\ 0)\), which is on \(b\). Two different parallel lines have no point in common. So, this is impossible.
Each of the other points gives a slanted line through the origin, and \(b\) can be the parallel line through \((4,\ 0)\).

steps.stem: A straight line passes through the origin and through \((m,\ n)\), where \(m>0\), \(n>0\) and \(m\ne n\). Which of the following points necessarily lies on the line?
explanation: On a line through the origin, both coordinates are multiplied by the same number.
\((m,\ n)\cdot(-3)=(-3m,\ {-}3n)\). So, this point is on the line.

Check the others with the ratio \(\frac xy\). The line has \(\frac mn\). \((2n,\ 2m)\) and \((\frac1m,\ \frac1n)\) both give \(\frac nm\), which is not \(\frac mn\) because \(m\ne n\). \((m,\ {-}n)\) gives a negative ratio.

Method 2 · Plugging in numbers: any \(m\ne n\) that are positive will do. Take \(m=1\), \(n=2\): the line goes through \((1,\ 2)\), so \(y=2x\). Only \((-3,\ {-}6)\) fits: \(-6=2\cdot(-3)\). \(\left(1,\ \frac12\right)\), \((4,\ 2)\) and \((1,\ {-}2)\) do not.

steps.stem: The point \(P(4,\ {-}3)\) is reflected across the \(x\)-axis to \(Q\). Then \(Q\) is reflected across the \(y\)-axis to \(R\). What is the length of \(PR\)?
explanation: Across the \(x\)-axis: \((x,\ y)\rightarrow(x,\ {-}y)\). So, \(Q=(4,\ 3)\).
Across the \(y\)-axis: \((x,\ y)\rightarrow(-x,\ y)\). So, \(R=(-4,\ 3)\). (Two reflections, one across each axis, are the same as a reflection through the origin.)
Trap: \(14=8+6\) adds the legs.

steps.stem: The line \(y=-2x+b\) passes through the point \((3,\ 1)\). At what point does the line intersect the \(x\)-axis?
explanation: Put the point into the equation: \(1=-2\cdot3+b\). So, \(b=7\). The line is \(y=-2x+7\).
The point is \((3.5,\ 0)\). Trap: \((0,\ 7)\) is where the line cuts the \(y\)-axis.

steps.stem: \(ABCDEF\) is a regular hexagon. \(AB\) lies on the positive \(x\)-axis, \(F\) lies on the positive \(y\)-axis, and \(B=(9,\ 0)\). A circle passes through all six vertices of the hexagon. What is the radius of the circle?
explanation: Let \(OA=x\). Each angle of a regular hexagon is \(120°\). So, \(\angle FAO=180°-120°=60°\).
Triangle \(FOA\) is a 30-60-90 triangle with short leg \(OA=x\). So, the side is \(AF=2x\).
\(AB=AF=2x\). So, \(OB=x+2x=3x=9\). Then \(x=3\) and the side is 6.
A regular hexagon is 6 equilateral triangles. So, the radius of the circle through its vertices equals the side: 6.

steps.stem: \(AOBC\) is a square in the first quadrant. \(O\) is the origin, and the sides \(OA\) and \(OB\) lie on the axes. The side of the square is \(4\). A circle centered at \(O\) passes through \(C\). What is the area of the part of the circle in the first quadrant that is outside the square?
explanation: The quarter of the circle in the first quadrant: \(\frac{32\pi}{4}=8\pi\).
Subtract the square, \(4^2=16\): \(8\pi-16\).

steps.stem: \(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle with \(AB=AC\). Given: \(B(-3,\ {-}1)\) and \(C(5,\ {-}1)\). \(A\) lies above \(BC\), and the area of the triangle is \(24\). What are the coordinates of \(A\)?
explanation: \(BC\) is horizontal: \(BC=5-(-3)=8\). Its midpoint is \(\left(\frac{-3+5}{2},\ {-}1\right)=(1,\ {-}1)\).
In an isosceles triangle, the altitude from \(A\) goes to the midpoint of \(BC\). So \(A\) has \(x=1\).

steps.stem: \(ABCD\) is a trapezoid with \(AD\parallel BC\). \(BC\) lies on the \(x\)-axis. The vertices \(A(0,\ k)\) and \(C(3k,\ 0)\) are given, where \(k>0\). \(D\) lies to the right of \(C\), and \(\angle ADC=60°\). What are the coordinates of \(D\)?
explanation: \(AD\parallel BC\) and \(BC\) is on the \(x\)-axis. So, \(AD\) is horizontal. \(D\) has the same \(y\) as \(A\): \(D=(x,\ k)\).
Drop \(DE\) to the \(x\)-axis: \(DE=k\). \(\angle DCE=\angle ADC=60°\), because they are alternate angles between the parallel lines \(AD\) and \(BC\).
Triangle \(CED\) is a 30-60-90 triangle. The leg \(DE=k\) faces the \(60°\) angle. So, the short leg is \(CE=\frac{k}{\sqrt3}\).
\(D=\left(3k+\frac{k}{\sqrt3},\ k\right)\). Trap: \((4k,\ k)\) treats the angle as \(45°\).

steps.stem: The vertices of quadrilateral \(ABCD\) are \(A(0,\ 2)\), \(B(5,\ 0)\), \(C(6,\ 4)\) and \(D(2,\ 6)\). What is the area of the quadrilateral?
explanation: Box: from \(x=0\) to \(x=6\) and from \(y=0\) to \(y=6\). Its area is \(6\cdot6=36\). Each vertex lies on a side of the box.
The four corner triangles: \(A\) to \(B\): \(\frac{5\cdot2}{2}=5\). \(B\) to \(C\): \(\frac{1\cdot4}{2}=2\). \(C\) to \(D\): \(\frac{4\cdot2}{2}=4\). \(D\) to \(A\): \(\frac{2\cdot4}{2}=4\).
